ordering_rules: Item 7 initial order is kept: W0 TPMC (admitted), W1 intake / design-state geometry sweep, W2 compressor design search / gaspath, W3 mission propagation, W4 UQ / Monte Carlo driver, W5 P3 ray sampling; then every remaining active Python execution path (W6-W20).
The migration does not stop after W5: the objective is ZERO Python execution dependency (item 7), so every component in the inventory is scheduled, including those with little speed benefit (item 6).
Profiling ORDERS the waves, it never GATES them (item 6): no Rust kernel may be blocked for lack of a per-kernel profiling result once the item-6 baseline is registered.

Re-prioritisation: the order of W1-W5 and of the remaining waves is re-ranked once the A9.24 item-6 pre-migration performance rerun is registered (status PENDING). Re-ranking may move waves earlier or later; it never removes a component and never changes a parity contract already registered.

Dependency closure: a Rust component may not call Python at runtime. When a component depends on a module scheduled in a later wave (pull_forward_required), that dependency is ported and admitted first under its own parity contract (pulled forward), never shimmed. W1E lists the enablers already known to be needed by W1-W5.
Evidence builders (W18) port after the physics crates they import are ADMITTED (depends_on_waves); until then they remain Python and keep producing the reference outputs.

Components marked HISTORICAL_LINE_OR_SUPERSEDED_CANDIDATE may be FORMALLY_RETIRED_NOT_PORTED instead of ported (item 14 'or has been formally retired'), only by an explicit owner/lane decision recorded in docs/HISTORY.md; their committed outputs stay as immutable evidence.
One component (or one tightly coupled group named in its contract) per parity contract; no big-bang wave admission (item 1).
Nothing in this order applies before the bid freeze (item 2 / item 9): every wave starts after the bid-freeze SHA is recorded.
